clue.text: Prophet needs a couple of seconds

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, in casual speech
S is the standard abbreviation for second(s)

explanation.surface: A seer is said to need only a moment or two.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'couple of seconds' are two different ways of writing a second: MO (as in 'half a mo') and the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a biblical book named after him.

clue.text: She's entitled to take a month to replace big beast's pound

indicators.note: to replace tells us one piece is swapped out of the big beast and another put in its place

parts.note: a lioness is a big cat, a big beast; the 's is a possessive link
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra
March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A titled woman somehow exchanges a month for part of a large animal.
explanation.walkthrough: In LIONESS the L (pound) is replaced by MARCH, giving MARCH-IONESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness holds a noble title, the wife of a marquess, so she is entitled in the literal sense.

clue.text: Symbolic way to take dictator's speech

definitions.text: Symbolic way to take dictator's speech

parts.words: Symbolic way to take dictator's speech
parts.note: a system of symbols used by secretaries to take down what a boss dictates, with 'dictator' read as one who dictates letters rather than a tyrant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a despot, but here it is simply someone dictating a letter to a stenographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenography uses abbreviated symbols so a secretary can record dictated speech at speaking pace.

clue.text: Good-natured, holding old way to be sustainable

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: affable means friendly and good-natured
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A kindly person keeping to an old path is somehow able to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good-natured' looks like part of the definition, but it is the outer piece; 'old way' fills it and 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something affordable can be supported or kept up financially, which is one sense of sustainable.

clue.text: Seized gold, capturing ship on sea

indicators.note: capturing means the gold takes the ship inside itself

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
SS stands for steamship
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Pirates grabbed treasure, taking a vessel on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seized' is past tense and so is the answer, as in 'assumed control'; 'on' is a link that places the sea last.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume power or control is to seize it, as when a ruler assumed the throne.

clue.text: Might it provide pensions to Tongans?

definitions.text: Might it provide pensions to Tongans?

parts.words: Might it provide pensions to Tongans?
parts.note: Tonga was named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook, so a mutual benefit society serving its people is jokingly given that islands' nickname

explanation.walkthrough: A friendly society is a British mutual association that provides benefits such as pensions and sickness pay; Tonga's old name was the Friendly Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual insurance clubs of this kind pay members pensions and sickness benefits in Britain.

clue.text: Dissolute type his conduct makes a lot of money

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Dissolute type his conduct makes a lot of money (5,2)': RAKE plus 'S plus SIN (his conduct) gives nine letters, not the seven of RAKES IN; no parse fits and a likely OCR or setting fault could not be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dissolute type his conduct makes a lot of money

clue.text: Cause to slow down in thicket

definitions.meaning: to apply a vehicle's stopping mechanism and so reduce speed
an old word for a clump of bracken or dense brushwood

explanation.surface: Something makes a traveller slow down inside dense undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to decelerate a vehicle and, archaically, a dense patch of scrub or fern.

clue.text: Expend energy, knocking over dinosaur

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocking over means the dinosaur is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: T rex, Tyrannosaurus rex, is the best-known dinosaur

explanation.surface: Someone uses a lot of energy toppling a dinosaur.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'knocking over' turns the dinosaur upside down, so it reads XERT beneath the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert effort or influence is to spend or apply it, so the verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: Potter's equipment obtained from plants with credit

parts.note: broom is a yellow-flowered shrub, so brooms are plants
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A craftsman's gear is bought from the garden centre on account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests a ceramics worker, but it is Harry Potter, who flies a broomstick. 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter rides a flying broom in Quidditch, making it his signature piece of kit.

clue.text: Mount semi-precious stone

definitions.meaning: a mount is a horse for riding
a green ornamental gemstone prized in Chinese carving

explanation.surface: A setting is offered for a modest gem.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a broken-down riding horse and a green hardstone used in jewellery.

clue.text: A musical essential — I got it from Gershwin

definitions.meaning: the regular beat and pattern of timing that music cannot do without
'I Got ___' is a famous 1930 song by George and Ira Gershwin

explanation.surface: Someone credits Gershwin for a key element of their music.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat and metre are basic to music, and the Gershwin song title is completed by the same word.

clue.text: Extremely unpleasant wine found in pleasant home

indicators.note: found in means the wine sits inside the home

parts.note: a nest, as in a cosy love-nest, is a snug home
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Something horrible to drink turns up in a lovely house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pleasant' sits inside a clue about unpleasantness, a deliberate contrast; it qualifies the home, which is a cosy one.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of nasty means the most disagreeable, matching 'extremely unpleasant'.

clue.text: Putting on cheerful aspect, raised breakfast order

parts.note: the sunny side of something is its cheerful aspect
up means lifted or raised

explanation.surface: Wearing a smile, someone orders breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on' is a link here, simply joining the pieces; in a down clue UP also sits below.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs fried on one side only with the yolk showing are ordered by this name at breakfast.

clue.text: Artist's meditative technique oddly swapped

indicators.note: oddly swapped means the odd-numbered letters, first and third, change places

parts.note: yoga is a meditative discipline of postures and breathing

explanation.surface: A painter's relaxation routine has been strangely altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly swapped' exchanges the first and third letters of YOGA, the Y and the G, giving GOY then A. 'Artist's' stands for 'Artist is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Lend ten quid, almost reforming young offender

indicators.note: reforming means the letters are formed afresh in a new order
almost means the last letter of quid is lost

explanation.surface: Lending a near-tenner to a teenage criminal might set them straight.
explanation.walkthrough: QUI is 'quid' less its last letter D; LEND TEN QUI is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A delinquent is a juvenile who commits crimes, a young offender in legal terms.

clue.text: Blind, not positioned to pick up sound

indicators.note: to pick up sound means we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: unsited means not placed or positioned

explanation.surface: Someone sightless is badly placed to hear anything.
explanation.walkthrough: UNSITED (not positioned) is said aloud to give the sight-related spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsighted means unable to see, especially when one's view is blocked, as in sport.

clue.text: Hope city goddess from Rome will reveal sacred writings

parts.note: Zenda is the fictional town in The Prisoner of Zenda by Anthony Hope
Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: Wishes for a town and a Roman deity will uncover holy texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' looks like a wish but is the novelist Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zend-Avesta is the body of Zoroastrian scripture with its commentary.

clue.text: Divers in France you must keep nearly dry

indicators.note: must keep means the French word holds the other piece inside

parts.note: vous is French for you

indicators.note: nearly means the word for dry is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: arid means dry

explanation.surface: Scuba enthusiasts in France are told to stay almost dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is not people diving but the old adjective meaning several; 'nearly' drops the last letter of the dry word, giving ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective divers means sundry or several, as does various.

clue.text: Like a ring? Girl maintains extremely unusual resistance

indicators.note: maintains means the girl's name holds the next letters within it

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of the word that follows

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A young woman shows remarkable endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: U and L, the first and last letters of 'unusual', go inside ANNA, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped, from Latin anulus, a little ring, as in an annular eclipse.

clue.text: Island sounds like heaven

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the sky, the heavens

explanation.surface: An island's name echoes paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is a large island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is one of the Inner Hebridean islands of Scotland.

clue.text: Murder penalty imposed on drunkard on drug is not generally understood

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the drunkard is written after the drug
imposed on means the fine is set after the drunkard on drug pair

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a sot is a habitual drunk
an eric was a fine paid in old Irish law by a killer to the victim's kin

explanation.surface: A drunk on drugs is hit with a murder fine, a story few people follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The eric was the old Irish blood-fine paid by a killer to the victim's family, little known outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is intended for or grasped only by a small inner circle.

clue.text: Half a chance rugby competition won't start

indicators.note: won't start means the rugby word loses its first letter

parts.note: sevens is a short form of rugby union played in tournaments

explanation.surface: A rugby tournament failing to begin leaves only a slim hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby sevens, seven-a-side rugby, loses its opening S. 'Half a chance' is not a slight chance but exactly fifty-fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens in betting means odds of one to one, a fifty per cent chance.

clue.text: Old province provided some good writing in the past

parts.note: the OT, the Old Testament, is part of the Good Book, the Bible
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A former region is said to have produced fine literature long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good writing' hints at the Good Book; some of it is the Old Testament. 'provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago was one of New Zealand's provinces until they were abolished in 1876, and remains a region.

clue.text: Passionate kissing without limits in spirited measure

indicators.note: without limits means the word for kissing loses its first and last letters

parts.note: snogging is British slang for kissing passionately

explanation.surface: A couple kissing passionately do so within a generous measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snogging' is British slang for a long kiss; its outer S and G go. 'Spirited' means of spirits, not lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small measure of spirits, traditionally a quarter of a pint.

clue.text: Thesaurus includes word for man tricked by kid brother

indicators.note: includes means the reference book holds the name inside its letters

explanation.surface: A book of synonyms lists a word for a man deceived by his sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' is apt twice over: Jacob was the younger twin, and he used kid goatskins to pose as his hairy brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Esau was cheated of his birthright and blessing by his younger twin Jacob.

clue.text: Use knife, perhaps, in widely-publicised protest

definitions.meaning: to slit an envelope with a paper knife is to unseal some mail
a letter of complaint addressed to someone but printed for all to read

explanation.surface: Someone takes a blade to their post in a very public complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the act of slitting an envelope and a published letter of protest.

clue.text: He warned Caesar, so to speak, in alternative case

indicators.note: in, together with case, means one word sits inside another
case means the outer word acts as a casing round the other

parts.note: other means alternative, as in the other choice
say means speak

explanation.surface: A prophet put it plainly in another set of circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' looks like a single phrase but splits; 'to' is a link. In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar the seer warns 'Beware the ides of March'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer, a fortune-teller, told Caesar to beware the ides of March.

clue.text: Weed perhaps needs to take some exercise

parts.note: to do a course is to take it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A weakling needs to get some physical activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' could be a feeble person or cannabis; dope fits both, as an idiot and as the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for cannabis, one kind of weed, hence the 'perhaps'.
